transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-29
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Morgan, Priya Shah (Redwood); Mike Duarte, Lina Park, Raj Patel, Ana Gomez (Sandbar)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and Sandbar Systems to explore OrbitBridge (Sandbar's marketplace/orchestration layer) as a GPU onramp for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments. Primary goals: confirm integration surface, security/compliance requirements, perf benchmarking plan, and pilot scope/timeline.

Topics covered:
- High-level architecture and where OrbitBridge would sit in customer infra
- Network/VPC requirements, private control plane options, and KMS/HSM integration
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and sample throughput targets for RLHF-like workloads
- Pilot success criteria and handoffs (security, infra, SRE owners)

---
00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the partnership side. With me is Priya Shah, our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Mike Duarte: Good, Alex. Thanks. I'm Mike, CTO at Sandbar. We have Lina and Raj here, and Ana the PM.
00:10 Priya Shah: Nice to meet you all. Quick agenda: intros, your goals with OrbitBridge and Redwood, then dive into integration points - networking, auth, perf, and pilot next steps. Sound good?
00:20 Lina Park: Yep, sounds good. We're pretty excited, we get lots of requests from customers wanting Redwood models through our marketplace and to slot into their private VPCs.
00:28 Raj Patel: For context, we run OrbitBridge as a thin orchestration layer in front of compute pools — both public cloud and on-prem blades. We do scheduling, cost-aware routing, and eject-to-fallback logic.
00:37 Alex Morgan: Perfect. The common patterns we see: routing to Redwood Hosted for small customers, Dedicated pools for mid-market, and Private for regulated workloads. We support a consistent API across all three.
00:47 Mike Duarte: The ask from our side: can OrbitBridge route to Redwood Dedicated/gpu pools and provide transparent model variant fallback if a preferred GPU type isn't available?
00:56 Priya Shah: Yes, that's feasible. We have model variant mapping and smart routing policies. One thing to align on: how you represent instance types and region tags in OrbitBridge, and how you'll call Redwood's routing APIs — we can accept region hints and cost-priority flags.
01:12 Ana Gomez: And on security: customers require private networking, audit logs, and KMS support. We have enterprise customers in finance and healthcare.
01:20 Alex Morgan: Understood. For Private deployments we can offer a customer-managed control plane that sits in their VPC or on-prem. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrapping, and we emit audit logs — Per-route traces and token-level telemetry in the Console.
01:34 Lina Park: Do you have an HSM connector or prefer KMS? A few customers mandate HSM-backed keys.
01:40 Priya Shah: We support both; typically KMS integrations are faster (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), but we can also integrate with HSM via PKCS#11 if needed. We'll want to capture key policies and who manages rotation.
01:52 Raj Patel: Network-wise, our scheduler needs to talk to the Redwood endpoints over private peering or VPN. Do you support VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink?
01:58 Alex Morgan: Both. For Hosted we use PrivateLink in regions that support it; for Private deployments everything is inside the customer's VPC so it's direct. For Dedicated, we can do peering or VLAN-based cross-connect depending on partner setup.
02:12 Mike Duarte: Great. On operational model: our customers expect single-pane billing and also unit costs to be visible in OrbitBridge. Can you surface per-token costs or a metering API?
02:22 Priya Shah: Yes, we have token-level cost and latency breakdown APIs; we can emit usage events that OrbitBridge can consume for billing. We'll need a quick schema exchange — we have a webhook spec and a usage export.
02:34 Alex Morgan: We'll drop the webhook spec in the integration doc.
02:36 (brief cross talk)
02:40 Alex Morgan: Let's talk perf. What's the workload profile you foresee? Short chat? Long-form generation? Batching patterns?
02:46 Lina Park: Most customers do chat + transient summarization. A couple have long-context retrieval-augmented generation for docs — so sequence lengths vary. Latency SLOs are 300-500ms for chat 95p, and throughput targets of ~200 concurrent sessions for larger customers.
03:02 Priya Shah: That's helpful. For that pattern, we'd recommend a mix: L4 quantized models for cost-sensitive routes, plus higher-precision variants for latency-sensitive or high-quality routes. Batching helps; our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache sharing for RAG. But it's workload dependent.
03:18 Raj Patel: On quant: do you support 4-bit quantization across the board? Some models degrade.
03:24 Priya Shah: We have recommended quant profiles per model in our catalog — we don't recommend 4-bit for some RLHF models. We'll provide model-by-model guidance in the doc. Also note that continuous batching and prefix KV cache can reduce overall cost while preserving latency for many RAG workflows.
03:41 Mike Duarte: For the pilot, we'd like a short run on one of our reference customers — can Redwood provide a dedicated pilot pool or are we expected to use Hosted?
03:50 Alex Morgan: For a partner pilot we typically spin up a small Dedicated pool for realistic throughput tests; that gives you isolation and we can instrument end-to-end Latency/Cost metrics. Alternatively, we can run a smaller test on Hosted to validate API and routing, then ramp to Dedicated.
04:03 Ana Gomez: Timeline-wise, we want something we can show in a Q3 partner launch window. So ideally pilot in June, evaluation in July, GA later in Q3.
04:12 Priya Shah: Feasible. Our standard pilot is 2-4 weeks of perf testing + security validation. We'll need a target workload, sample prompts, and an SLA matrix.
04:22 Alex Morgan: Action item: we'll share a pilot checklist and perf metric sheet — that's part of the integration package.

04:30 04:30 Mike Duarte: Quick question on model variants and fallbacks: if OrbitBridge asks for Redwood-XL on A100 and it's full, can we fallback to Redwood-XL-quant on a different instance type automatically?
04:39 Priya Shah: Yes, that's our typical fallback chain. You can define policy knobs: prefer low-latency, prefer cost, region-only, etc. We'll return a 1xx advisory then route. Worth noting: generated outputs may differ with quantized variants; you'll want regression tests and eval prompt sets.
04:55 Raj Patel: About metrics: is token-level tracing a PII or data sensitivity problem? We want to avoid storing user text.
05:02 Alex Morgan: Good point. We have configurable telemetry levels. You can capture only token counts, latency, and anonymized traces. For regulated customers we support a no-PII mode where payloads are never persisted in the control plane.
05:14 Lina Park: Ok, send the config options.

05:20 05:20 Alex Morgan: Security and compliance — what do you need from our side?
05:23 Mike Duarte: SOC2, ISO, pen test reports, and data residency options. Also SSO integration for OrbitBridge admin portal to manage routing.
05:31 Priya Shah: We'll attach our SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, and pen test summary in the security package. For SSO we support SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC via our Console; you can provision OrbitBridge service accounts or use an org-level SSO mapping.
05:45 Raj Patel: For KMS, we need key-wrapping in our HSM; can Redwood call our KMS endpoints?
05:50 Priya Shah: In Private mode, Redwood control plane runs in-customer VPC so calls to your KMS are native. For Dedicated we can set up a secure connector; we'll need details on network egress rules and certs.
06:03 06:03 Ana Gomez: Anything else from the infra side?
06:06 Raj Patel: One more: logging retention. Partners sometimes want 90 days, enterprise 365. Are retention windows configurable?
06:13 Alex Morgan: Yes, retention is configurable per-account under our Console; some longer-term retention is an add-on. We'll call that out in the pricing and compliance sections.

06:24 06:24 Priya Shah: I'd like to propose a small technical spike: we'll run a 48-hour throughput test with 100 concurrent RAG sessions on a small Dedicated pool to collect latency percentiles, token-cost, and KV cache hit rates. That will help size the instance types and batching configs for OrbitBridge.
06:38 Mike Duarte: That sounds good. Can Redwood instrument and produce a CSV we can import to OrbitBridge to simulate routing?
06:44 Priya Shah: Yes — we'll produce a sample metrics CSV and explain the column mapping. We'll also provide a Perf-run script and a Dockerized load generator if you want to run from your infra.
06:55 Alex Morgan: On the billing side, we'll provide estimated unit economics for the pilot: per-token cost, estimated infra, and a pilot invoice model. OrbitBridge can map usage events to its billing pipeline.
07:08 07:08 Lina Park: Competitor check — a few customers asked us about CloudFast's integration. How is Redwood differentiated?
07:14 Alex Morgan: Two things: production latency guarantees and model lifecycle control. We provide first-class observability and rollout policies so you can pin a model version and perform canary rollouts across customers. Also, our Optimize product recommends quant and batching configs based on your workload to hit cost targets.
07:29 Mike Duarte: Any gotchas?
07:31 Priya Shah: The main one is model output drift when switching quant variants — which is why we recommend running evals on prompt sets before enabling auto-fallback. Also, private deployments require some infra setup time — usually 2-3 weeks for staffed integration depending on network approvals.
07:47 Raj Patel: That's fine. We'll plan for a staged rollout.

07:52 07:52 Alex Morgan: Ok, so to recap next steps: Alex share integration doc + webhook schema and billing export; Priya share perf checklist and runbook; Sandbar to share compliance contact and timeline. We'll aim for a pilot setup in early June.
08:05 Ana Gomez: I'll coordinate calendar invites and loop in our security lead for the SOC2 deep-dive.
08:10 Mike Duarte: Great summary. Anything else?
08:13 Priya Shah: One small note: for routing we recommend adding a route tag for 'sensitivity' to separate PII-sensitive traffic which can force no-persist mode.
08:22 Raj Patel: Good idea. We'll add that to the schema.

08:28 08:28 Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone. I'll send the doc and spreadsheet after this call. Priya, anything to add?
08:33 Priya Shah: Just that we'll propose instance types in the doc — GA100-ish and some cost-focused T4-style fallback configs — and we'll include the quant recommendations per model.
08:44 Mike Duarte: Perfect. Thanks.
08:46 Meeting end.

Notes / artifacts referenced:
- Integration doc (to be shared): architecture.md, webhook-spec.yaml, billing-schema.csv
- Perf spreadsheet: sandbar-redwood-pilot-metrics.csv (will be shared by Alex)
- Security package: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, pen-test summary (to be attached)

Transcript quirks observed:
- "KV cache" transcribed as "KV cash" a couple places in automated notes
- Occasional speaker mislabels near crosstalk at 03:50-04:03
- Proper nouns sometimes imperfect: OrbitBridge was occasionally transcribed as "Orbit Bridge" (space)

Pilot framing (explicit success criteria suggested during call):
- 48-hour perf run hitting 200 concurrent sessions with 95p latency < 500ms for chat route OR documented tradeoff if not achievable
- CSV with token cost and latency breakdowns imported into OrbitBridge simulation
- Security sign-off: SOC2 artefacts reviewed and no-PII mode validated on a test request

End of transcript.
